sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 59-106. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 60: 'At least one language, Shen, has lost all trace of nominal affixes and has compensated by evolving a complex tonal inventory.' Section 3.2 (p. 69) on Shen covers only nominal morphology (no plural or plural suffix ba(u)) and Busa influence.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria (Comparative Kainji: main text, circulation draft, 11 May 2012). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 3.2.2 'Shen [Laru]' (p. 8) gives only sources, dialects, villages and Busa influence; chapter 4 'Phonology' has subsections for Reshe, Shuba, Rop, Proto-Lake but none for Shen, and those are empty headings in this draft. Shen forms in the comparative wordlists are tone-marked (e.g. yábà 'skin', mèmbí 'eye', púnà 'leg'). No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' anywhere in the 643 KB text.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart & Roger Blench. 2012. Documentation, development, and ideology in the northwestern Kainji languages. Language Documentation and Description 11: 90-135.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Open-access survey of NW Kainji including the Lake group; sociolinguistic in focus, so only a slim chance of a prosodic remark on Shen.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. The Lopa language of Northwestern Nigeria and its affinities (draft circulated for comment, 2 June 2006). Cambridge: Mallam Dendo.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology chapter (vowels, consonants, tones) is about Lopa only; Laru appears only as tone-marked comparanda in the wordlist (e.g. 'cf. Laru yàBí', 'cf. Laru swàrú') and in the remark that Lopa's 'nearest relative is Laru, unfortunately a poorly known language'. Nothing on Laru stress.
